title: Oak Watch onboarding — raw implementation jot
content:
Purpose: working notes from intake and technical scoping for Oak Watch (industrial CCTV analytics vendor). Raw — action items + open questions. Not polished; for internal handoff to eng + private deployments team.

1) Quick summary
- Customer: Oak Watch Inc — OEM of edge cameras + centralized analytics. Wants Redwood to host inference for event detection and also provide a private-deploy option for regulated customers.
- Primary ask: low-latency object/behavior classification for security alerts (avg inference window < 300ms p50, 500ms p95), support for batched ingestion from edge gateways, and redaction/PII handling for footage metadata.
- Preferred deployment: start hosted API for rapid POC, move to Private (VPC) for pilot with two enterprise customers.

2) Attendees (2025-07-21 call)
- Oak Watch: Maria Gomez (CTO), Ben Liu (Edge Ops), Claire Donovan (Security Lead)
- Redwood: Sofia Martinez (SE, owner), Daniel Park (eng liasion), Priya Singh (private deployments lead)

3) Technical constraints and notes
- Edge gateways send protobuf messages over TLS to forwarder cluster; typical payload is metadata + small base64 clip (1s, 480p) or reference URL (S3).
- Throughput: during shifts, expected burst of 800 requests/min per site, typical steady 120 requests/min. Pilot will cover 3 sites initially.
- Payload size caps: customer wants 2MB cap for direct uploads. We need to confirm Redwood hosted API default body limits and multipart support.
- Latency SLO: see summary above. Must measure end-to-end (gateway -> Redwood -> model -> webhook back).
- Security: customer requires AES256 envelope encryption at rest, and HSM-backed KMS for private deploy. Logs must be redactable; they want PII scrub rules applied before storage.
- Models: primarily vision models they have trained (ONNX / TorchScript). They prefer bringing their custom model, but may trial Redwood-curated multi-modal classifiers. Need clarity on supported model formats for Private.

4) Gotchas & risks called out in call
- On-prem cameras sometimes lose connectivity and replay old clips — need dedup/TTL semantics on ingestion to avoid repeated charges and duplicate alerts.
- Customer's enterprise sites block outbound traffic to unknown hosts; Private deployment will likely be required for those sites.
- Model formats: Oak Watch uses custom ops in Torch that may not be compatible with Redwood runtime without dockerized runtime extensions — escalate to runtime team to validate.
- Cost expectation mismatch: Oak Watch expects low per-request cost for real-time; our Dedicated/private pricing examples suggested earlier may under-estimate the burst cost. Flag to pricing.

5) Proposed POC approach (minimal friction)
- Phase A (2 weeks): Hosted API POC using a small sample dataset. Implement ingestion adaptor on their gateway to call Redwood hosted endpoint with sample clips (N=500/day). Measure latency and basic throughput.
- Phase B (4–6 weeks): Private VPC deployment for two enterprise sites (pilot). Bring their TorchScript model artifacts. Work with infra to provision 2x g4dn-equivalent instances with autoscale triggers.
- Phase C (3 months): Harden redaction pipeline, integrate KMS/HSM, compliance audit for SOC2/PCI as required by customer.

6) Immediate action items (owners + ETA)
- Sofia: send POC onboarding checklist and sample ingestion adapter (node/python) by 2025-07-23.
- Daniel: spike on custom Torch ops compatibility and report by 2025-07-28 (create GitHub repo for test model).
- Priya: draft Private deployment manifest template and preliminary cost estimate for pilot (2025-07-30).
- Sales: schedule executive sponsor intro w/ Oak Watch leadership (by 2025-07-27).
- Security: propose redaction transformation rules and sample pipeline (by 2025-07-29).

7) Open questions for Oak Watch (to resolve before Phase B)
- Can they export a small representative model (with dummy weights) that reproduces custom ops so runtime can validate?
- Are their enterprise sites ok with outbound traffic to Redwood control plane during Private deploy? If not, on-prem airgapped path needed.
- Expected retention window for logs/alerts and compliance regime per site (SOC2? local privacy laws).
- Are they ok with initial sampling approach (hosted POC) for latency numbers, or do they insist on starting Private?

8) Notes on integration specifics
- Webhook pattern: model results should be posted back to customer webhook; for high throughput consider streaming responses vs single webhook per batch.
- Caching: many events are prefix-similar (repeated frames); consider prefix/KV caching to reduce repeat compute—ask runtime if image-hash-based cache hooks feasible.
- Batching: adaptive batching recommended for cost. We will need to tune batch size to meet p95 latency target; include continuous batching policy in POC.

9) Internal flags / who to loop in
- Eng runtime: Daniel to loop in Maya Chen (inference-kernel) on custom ops complexity.
- Private deploys infra: Priya to loop in Kunal Reddy for HSM/KMS integration constraints.
- Pricing: loop in Alex Rivera for draft pilot quote and long-term pricing template.

10) Next meeting: scheduling notes
- Proposed cadence: weekly 30-min stand for first 4 weeks. Next sync penciled: 2025-07-28 14:00 PT (Sofia to confirm).

Quick scratch extras:
- Slack thread: #cust-oak-watch (created) — drop snippets of call and the POC checklist.
- Quick wins: offer a prebuilt prometheus exporter for gateway metrics and default Grafana dashboard for alert latency.

Raw capture ends — keep this page for iterative notes and handoff.
